extracted.intended_audience: Toastmasters contest chairs, chief judges, voting/tiebreaking judges, timers, counters, contestants, and other contest officials
extracted.subtask_description: Official rulebook guidance for planning, conducting, and judging Toastmasters speech contests (International, Humorous, Evaluation, Table Topics, Tall Tales, and Online), including timing, equipment, eligibility, protests, use of props, video submission, and role checklists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signaling device and backup timer requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A signaling device that displays green, yellow, and red colors must be used; for the Online Speech Contest, a minimum of one (1) backup timer is also appointed in case of any technical difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signaling device must be in full view of each contestant. If the timer operating the signaling device is unable to complete their role, a backup timer must be ready to operate the signaling device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timer record is official time
rubrics_metrics.description: The timer with the stopwatch maintains and delivers to the chief judge the written record of elapsed time of each speech on the Speech Contest Time Record Sheet and Instructions for Timers (Item 1175). This constitutes the official time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must not consider fractions of a second when determining qualification/disqualification boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timer must ensure accurate, visible signals
rubrics_metrics.description: The timer managing the timing device ensures that contestants are able to view an accurate green, yellow, or red signal at appropriate times during the speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must provide warning signals to the contestants which must be clearly visible to the speakers but not obvious to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: International/Humorous/Online contest timing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: International, Humorous, and Online contest speeches must be from five (5) to seven (7) minutes. A contestant will be disqualified if the speech is less than four (4) minutes 30 seconds or more than seven (7) minutes 30 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must not consider fractions of a second. A contestant is not qualified until their time reaches four (4) minutes and 30 seconds and is not disqualified until their time reaches seven (7) minutes and 31 seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table Topics contest timing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Table Topics Contest speeches must be from one (1) minute to two (2) minutes. A contestant will be disqualified if the speech is less than one (1) minute or more than two (2) minutes 30 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must not consider fractions of a second. A contestant is not qualified until their time reaches one (1) minute and is not disqualified until their time reaches two (2) minutes and 31 seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation contest timing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation Contest speeches must be from two (2) to three (3) minutes. A contestant will be disqualified if the speech is less than one (1) minute 30 seconds or more than three (3) minutes 30 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must not consider fractions of a second. A contestant is not qualified until their time reaches one (1) minute and 30 seconds and is not disqualified until their time reaches three (3) minutes and 31 seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tall Tales contest timing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Tall Tales Contest speeches must be from three (3) to five (5) minutes. A contestant will be disqualified if the speech is less than two (2) minutes 30 seconds or more than five (5) minutes 30 seconds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must not consider fractions of a second. A contestant is not qualified until their time reaches two (2) minutes and 30 seconds and is not disqualified until their time reaches five (5) minutes and 31 seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestant must proceed immediately after introduction and AV check
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being introduced, the contestant must proceed immediately to the speaking position and, to ensure audiovisual equipment is functional, must say, 'Thank you, Contest Chair.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If AV is functional the chair replies 'You're welcome' and timing begins with the contestant’s next definite verbal or nonverbal communication (e.g., next word, sound effect, staged act). If AV is not functional the contest chair will notify the contestant and pause the contest to allow corrections; for Online contests a contestant is allowed 10 minutes to attempt corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning signal schedule (per contest type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timers must provide green/yellow/red signals at specified times depending on contest type so signals are visible to speakers but not obvious to audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International/Humorous/Online: green at 5:00 for 1 minute, yellow at 6:00 for 1 minute, red at 7:00 until conclusion. Evaluation: green at 2:00 for 30 sec, yellow at 2:30 for 30 sec, red at 3:00 until conclusion. Table Topics: green at 1:00 for 30 sec, yellow at 1:30 for 30 sec, red at 2:00 until conclusion. Tall Tales: green at 3:00 for 1 minute, yellow at 4:00 for 1 minute, red at 5:00 until conclusion. In all speech contests, no signal can be given for the overtime period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodations for visually impaired contestants
rubrics_metrics.description: Any visually impaired contestant is permitted to request and must be granted a form of warning signal of their own choosing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable warning signals include, but are not limited to: a buzzer, a bell, or a person announcing the times at five (5), six (6), and seven (7) minutes. If any special device/instructions are required, the contestant must provide them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical failure of signal/timing equipment — extra overtime allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of technical failure of the signal or timing equipment, a speaker is allowed 30 seconds extra overtime before being disqualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of time disqualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to announcing results, the contest chair must announce the number of time disqualifications, but not name the contestant(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disqualifications for originality, referencing another contestant, or not presenting a new/different semifinal/final speech are not announced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests: scope, who may lodge, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests are limited to eligibility, originality, and reference to another contestant or another contestant’s speech and must only be lodged by voting judges and/or contestants. Any protest must be lodged with the chief judge and/or contest chair prior to the contest being adjourned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chief judge, contest chair, voting judges, and contestants must not consider protests from audience members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure before disqualification for originality/reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a contestant can be disqualified on the basis of originality, or for referencing another contestant’s speech, the contestant must be given an opportunity to respond to the voting judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A majority of the voting judges must concur in the decision to disqualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest chair authority to disqualify for eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest chair can disqualify a contestant on the basis of eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure eligibility checks are done before the contest; eligibility-related disqualifications should be handled prior to the contest when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of props and electronic devices notification and venue compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants who plan to use props (including electronic devices, music, PowerPoint slides, or virtual backgrounds) must notify the contest chair prior to the contest and must abide by any venue restrictions on the use of props.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All props must be set up during the minute of silence prior to the contestant’s speech and removed in the minute of silence following the speech. Contestants may enlist someone to help but it is not the responsibility of contest officials. Contestants must demonstrate prior to the contest that props can be set up and removed in allotted times; failure to demonstrate means props cannot be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Speech Contest: English and originality purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Speech Contest must be conducted in English only and every speech should 'clearly develop and present ideas in a substantially original speech.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows General Rules; additional requirements apply for video submissions and advancement through levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-level video technical requirements for International contest
rubrics_metrics.description: District-level contest videos submitted to World Headquarters must meet detailed audio, camera, lighting, and recording requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio must be clear without echo/static. Camera must record in high definition, be single-camera only (no multiple angles), be on a tripod, have unobstructed in-focus view of contestant, entire speaking area visible throughout, be monitored by an operator at all times, and zooming is not permitted. Lighting: speaking area fully lit, facial expressions visible, image not too bright/dark, and no lighting should point directly at the camera. Video may contain only the introduction of the winning contestant’s speech and the entire winning speech and may not be edited (no added text/graphics/images).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failing quarterfinal video requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a quarterfinal video fails to meet any recording requirements, the contestant will be disqualified by the chief judge; the submitting District will be notified and given three (3) business days to submit the next highest-placed contestant’s video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second submission of the first contestant is not permitted. If the next submission fails, that contestant is disqualified and no additional opportunities are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterfinal judging procedure for video contests
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarterfinal judges view submitted videos under strict conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges will view all videos for their assigned contest in the order provided by the chief judge, must view all videos in one (1) sitting, may only view each video once, and pausing or rewinding is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: World Championship speech newness requirement and qualifying process
rubrics_metrics.description: Every participant in the World Championship of Public Speaking must present an entirely new and different speech than presented during that year's semifinal or any previous year's semifinal and final-round speeches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semifinal winners prepare and deliver outlines of semifinal speeches to World Headquarters. Qualifying judges receive outlines and a qualification sheet to indicate whether the World Championship speech is new/different. If three (3) of five (5) qualifying judges mark Disqualified for a speaker, that speaker is disqualified and no protest may be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version of rulebook in effect for semifinals and World Championship
rubrics_metrics.description: The semifinals and World Championship will follow the version of the rulebook that was in effect when the contest cycle began on the previous July 1 (approximately 14 months before the World Championship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Contest: test speech and preparation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of the Evaluation contest, a five (5)- to seven (7)-minute test speech will be presented; it must be a contest-type speech or a project speech from Toastmasters Pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants may make preparatory notes using the Evaluation Contestant Notes sheet (Item 1177) and have five (5) minutes to prepare after leaving the room (or prepare in-room under supervision if impractical to leave). The test speaker should preferably not be a member of the same club as any contestant. The test speaker must be introduced by announcing the speaker’s name, speech title, speech title, and the speaker’s name. Neither the test speaker’s project nor objectives may be made known to contestants, judges, tiebreaking judge, or audience. No digital devices may be used to gain an unfair advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Contest notes handling and introduction format
rubrics_metrics.description: After five (5) minutes, no further preparation is allowed and contestants must hand their Evaluation Contestant Notes sheet to the Sergeant at Arms; notes are returned as contestants are introduced. Introduce each contestant by announcing the contestant’s name twice (Evaluation speeches do not have titles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous Speech Contest content and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject for the Humorous Contest speech must be selected by the contestant; the speaker must avoid potentially objectionable language, anecdotes, and material. The speech must be thematic in nature (opening, body, and close), not a monologue (series of one-liners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Table Topics Contest topic and delivery rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All contestants must receive the same topic of a general nature selected by the contest chair; the topic must be reasonable length, not require detailed knowledge, and must lead to an opinion or conclusion. Contestants receive no advance knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During contest, when contest begins all contestants except the first must leave the room and remain under supervision. Introduce each contestant by announcing: contestant’s name, the topic, the topic, the contestant’s name. Contestants must not use digital or other devices to gain an unfair advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tall Tales Contest subject and use of props
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tall Tales speech must be of a highly exaggerated, improbable nature and have a theme or plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor and props may be used to support or illustrate the speech, subject to general props rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Speech Contest: live participation and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Online Speech Contest is conducted with all contestants and contest officials participating live, online from physically distant locations; all participants must participate live, in real-time, using equipment they obtain themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All briefings and rehearsals must be conducted online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online contest briefings and rehearsals content
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants’ briefing and judge’s briefing must include guidance on how technical difficulties will be addressed, how participants can contact chief judge/contest chair/moderators, and how chief judge/contest chair can communicate with participants during the contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearsal must include each contestant conducting an audiovisual check and the contest chair defining each contestant’s speaking area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online platform functional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform selected for hosting the Online Speech Contest must meet specific requirements so all contestants and officials can participate effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: All contestants can join with ability to turn video on/off and mute/unmute; all contest officials can view contestant speeches live while maintaining confidentiality; the host can mute participants, turn off video, and prompt participants to unmute/turn on video; all contestants can receive timing signals from the timer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online contest pause/communication protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the contest, the chief judge and contest chair establish a way to privately communicate or signal that the contest should be paused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Online Speech Contest Statement about privacy/recording must be read or posted visibly to all participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online contestant technical difficulty procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contestant experiences a technical difficulty (audio/video severely weakened or lost), the chief judge and contest chair confer and determine whether the contest is paused; if paused the impacted contestant is allowed no more than 10 minutes to attempt to reestablish a secure connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If connection is reestablished within 10 minutes, the contest chair indicates the last word/sentence heard and contestant continues from that point with no additional time allowance. If unable to reestablish within 10 minutes, the contest continues with the next contestant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge technical difficulty and backup judge procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a voting judge experiences a technical difficulty and cannot hear/see sufficiently, they must notify the chief judge immediately and their ballot will not be included in final results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backup judges may be appointed prior to the contest to serve in case of technical difficulty. If appointed, backups must judge the entire contest but their ballot will only be consulted if a primary judge was unable to complete their role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timer technical difficulty and backup timer procedure (online)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timer experiences a technical difficulty and cannot hear/see sufficiently, they must notify the chief judge immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The backup timer must time all speeches but their Time Record Sheet will only be consulted from the point at which the primary timer was unable to complete their role. If there is only one backup timer, they must also be ready to operate the signaling device if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause/reschedule rules for widespread technical difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: If enough contest participants experience technical difficulty such that the contest cannot proceed, the chief judge and contest chair determine whether to pause the contest; if paused it must be resumed within one (1) hour or the remainder rescheduled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If paused and resumed within one hour, a contestant partway through resumes from the last heard word with no additional time. If rescheduled, only contestants who have not yet presented will present during the rescheduled contest; a contestant partway through may begin from the start during the rescheduled contest. Contest officials must send partially completed forms to the chief judge to be stored until the rescheduled contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on external voting systems
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of external voting systems is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest planning and Contest Chair responsibilities (checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest chair must plan the contest budget; make arrangements for venue/online platform/audiovisual equipment; conduct pre- and post-contest publicity; ensure bills are paid; ensure each speaker is eligible and familiar with rules; ensure contest officials are briefed; ensure ballots are counted carefully; and ensure awards are presented appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although committee help is allowed, ultimate responsibility remains with the contest chair. Entry fees to attend must be waived for contestants; contestants cannot be charged a fee to compete. Provide contestants with an information packet (rulebook, forms, training materials) 2–6 weeks before contest. Verify eligibility using tools (Eligibility Assistant) and education requirements for International contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestants' briefing and preparation checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants' briefing must verify presence and pronunciation of names, review rules, review Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality, review timing protocol, acquaint contestants with exact speaking area, determine speaking positions, and ensure contestants are comfortable with the platform for Online contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For International/Evaluation/Humorous/Table Topics/Tall Tales contests this may include lectern, tables, lighting, microphone, etc. All contestants must have opportunity to test amplifying equipment. For Online contests, contest chair works with each contestant to test audio/video and set a standard speaking area.

rubrics_metrics.name: During-contest duties for Contest Chair
rubrics_metrics.description: Open contest with a brief introduction stating rules were reviewed, location of timing lights, prohibition of photography, and noting that speeches may contain sensitive content; introduce each speaker without preliminary remarks including club name/location; confirm audiovisual equipment is functional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After speeches, ask judges to complete ballots, collect ballots and Time Record Sheets, ensure forms kept confidential, interview each speaker while ballots counted, collect results from chief judge, address protests before adjournment, and announce if time disqualification(s) occurred without naming individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief Judge and Judge briefing and counting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief judge appoints and counsels voting judges, counters, timers; provides counters with Counter’s Tally Sheet; encourages officials to view online training; conducts judge’s briefing; determines method of private communication with contest chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge’s briefing must distribute list of contestants, Judge’s Guide and Ballot, Rulebook, Judge’s Certification and Code of Ethics, and any training materials. Instruct judges on protocol to mitigate unexpected challenges. Oversee counting process and ensure all ballots are counted twice. Ensure confidentiality and proper disposal of contest forms and do not discuss details of protests/disqualifications (except eligibility) with contestants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestant responsibilities before/during/after their speech (checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before contest: select a substantially original speech (for certain contests), attend briefings and rehearsal, inform contest chair of props, review eligibility and originality certification. During contest: set up props in one minute of silence before introduction, say 'Thank you, Contest Chair' after introduction and begin when chair replies, check timing signals regularly and wrap up on red, remove props immediately after speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants may enlist help with props but contest officials are not responsible. For online contests secure and test audiovisual equipment. Review Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality (Item 1183) and sign to certify understanding.
